(1) a Bayesian classifier can be trained on the fly, using a zoomable browser, to filter out articles not of interest to a user, based on his profile; (2) the profile can be updated on the fly, based on the user's reading behaviors; (3) the user can easily change the profile to suit his current needs, by changing the weight of the profile's components; and (4) the system is able to infer the user's interest in a particular article

1) the system is able to select articles of potential interest to a user, based on a Bayesian classification algorithm, 2) the system is robust enough to adapt to a user's changing interests, 3) the system is accurate in inferring a user's interest in a particular article, and 4) the system is efficient in terms of computational resources.

the system is able to: (1) classify news articles with a high degree (over 90%) of accuracy, (2) adapt to a user's interests in less than ten readings, and (3) provide a user with a zoomable interface to browse the news articles.
